title: H-1B Worker RSU Double Taxation When Returning to Canada: Complete Guide 2026
description: Avoid double taxation on RSUs when transitioning from H-1B in the US back to Canada. Learn how Foreign Tax Credit works, tax treaty benefits, and step-by-step filing process.
content:
## Key Takeaways

- **Double taxation is avoidable** through proper Foreign Tax Credit (FTC) claims
- H-1B workers returning to Canada face taxation in **both countries** on unvested RSUs
- The US-Canada tax treaty provides relief but doesn't eliminate filing requirements
- Average savings: **$8,000-$15,000** annually with proper FTC optimization
- Use our [free US-Canada RSU tax calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) to calculate exact liability

## The Double Taxation Problem for Returning H-1B Workers

You worked 3 years at Amazon Seattle on H-1B. You received a 4-year $240K RSU grant ($60K/year). Now you're moving back to Toronto for family reasons.

**The trap:** Your 4th-year RSUs will vest *after* you become a Canadian tax resident. Both countries want to tax the same income:

- **United States:** Claims tax because you *earned* the RSUs while working in Seattle
- **Canada:** Claims tax because you're a *resident* when RSUs vest

**Without proper planning, you could pay:**
- US tax: $22,000 (22% federal withholding + 10% state)
- Canada tax: $21,000 (35% marginal rate on CAD equivalent)
- **Total: $43,000 on $60,000 income** = 71.7% effective tax rate

## How the US-Canada Tax Treaty Prevents Double Taxation

Article XV of the US-Canada Tax Treaty allocates RSU taxation rights based on where you **performed the work**, not where you live when they vest.

### Work Period Attribution Formula

```
US Taxable Amount = Total RSU Value × (Days worked in US / Total vesting period days)
Canada Taxable Amount = Total RSU Value × (Days worked in Canada / Total vesting period days)
```

**Example:** 4-year RSU grant, worked 3 years in US, 1 year in Canada
- Total vesting period: 1,460 days
- Days in US: 1,095 days (75%)
- Days in Canada: 365 days (25%)
- $60K vesting: US gets $45K, Canada gets $15K

### But There's a Catch: US Withholding Doesn't Care About Treaties

Your employer (Amazon, Google, Meta, etc.) will withhold **22% on the entire $60K** = $13,200, even though the treaty says only $45K is US-taxable.

**What happens:**
1. US withholds $13,200 on $60K
2. You file US Form 1040-NR claiming treaty benefit
3. US refunds $3,300 (excess withholding on $15K)
4. You claim $9,900 Foreign Tax Credit in Canada
5. Canada taxes $60K but gives credit for US tax paid

## Step-by-Step: How to Avoid Double Taxation

### Step 1: Track Your Work Location Days

**Critical:** Keep a **daily log** of where you physically worked.

**Why:** Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and IRS *will* ask for proof during audits. Use:
- Passport stamps (entry/exit dates)
- Employer badge swipe records
- Flight itineraries
- Calendar screenshots showing office location

**Pro Tip:** Create a simple spreadsheet:

| Date | Location | Days Count |
|------|----------|------------|
| Jan 1-Dec 31, 2023 | Seattle, WA | 365 |
| Jan 1-Dec 31, 2024 | Seattle, WA | 365 |
| Jan 1-Dec 31, 2025 | Seattle, WA | 365 |
| Jan 1-Dec 31, 2026 | Toronto, ON | 365 |
| **Total** | | **1,460** |

### Step 2: Determine Your Tax Residency Status

**You become a Canadian tax resident when you:**
- Establish a "permanent home" in Canada (buy/rent)
- Have "significant residential ties" (spouse, dependents in Canada)
- Spend 183+ days in Canada in the calendar year

**You cease US tax residency when:**
- Your H-1B expires and you leave the US
- You file Form I-407 (abandoning green card, if applicable)
- You don't meet Substantial Presence Test (183 days)

**Dual-status year:** The year you move, you're a US resident for part of the year, Canadian resident for the rest. File:
- US: Form 1040-NR (dual-status statement attached)
- Canada: T1 return with departure date noted

### Step 3: Calculate US vs Canada Tax Allocation

Use our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) or manually:

**Example: Meta 4-year RSU grant**
- Grant date: Jan 1, 2023
- Total value: $240K ($60K/year)
- Work period: 3 years US, 1 year Canada
- Vesting dates: 25% each year on Jan 1

**Year 4 vesting (Jan 1, 2026):**
- Total vested: $60,000
- US portion: $60K × (1,095 days / 1,460 days) = $45,000
- Canada portion: $60K × (365 days / 1,460 days) = $15,000

### Step 4: File US Form 1040-NR with Treaty Claim

**Key forms:**
- **Form 1040-NR** (US Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return)
- **Schedule NEC** (Tax on Income Not Effectively Connected)
- **Form 8833** (Treaty-Based Return Position Disclosure)

**How to claim treaty benefit:**

On Schedule NEC:
1. Report $45,000 (US-sourced portion) as wages
2. Do NOT report $15,000 (Canada-sourced portion)
3. Attach Form 8833 explaining Article XV treaty position

**Form 8833 sample language:**
> "I am claiming a treaty-based return position under Article XV of the US-Canada Income Tax Treaty. The $15,000 of RSU income attributable to services performed in Canada is exempt from US taxation per Article XV(1)."

**Pro Tip:** The IRS will withhold the full $13,200. You'll get a $3,300 refund when you file 1040-NR.

### Step 5: File Canadian T1 with Foreign Tax Credit

**Key forms:**
- **T1 General** (Canadian Income Tax Return)
- **T2209** (Federal Foreign Tax Credits)
- **Schedule 1** (Federal Tax)

**How to claim Foreign Tax Credit:**

1. **Report full $60,000 CAD equivalent:**
   - $60,000 USD × 1.36 FX rate = $81,600 CAD
   - Enter on Line 10400 (Employment Income)

2. **Calculate Canada tax:**
   - Federal: 29% on income over $111,733
   - Ontario: 11.16% on income over $80,000
   - Total: ~35% marginal rate = $28,560 CAD

3. **Claim Foreign Tax Credit:**
   - US tax paid: $9,900 USD = $13,464 CAD
   - Enter on Form T2209
   - Credit reduces Canada tax to $15,096 CAD

**Net result:**
- US tax: $9,900 (on $45K)
- Canada tax: $15,096 (on $60K minus FTC)
- **Total: $25,000 vs $43,000 without treaty** = $18,000 savings

## Common Mistakes That Cost Thousands

### Mistake 1: Not Filing Form 8833

If you claim treaty benefits reducing US tax by >$500, you **must** file Form 8833 or face a **$1,000 penalty**.

### Mistake 2: Using Wrong FX Rate for FTC

Canada requires you to use the **Bank of Canada average annual exchange rate** for the year, not the rate on vesting day.

**Where to find it:** [Bank of Canada FX rates](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/exchange/annual-average-exchange-rates/)

**2026 rate:** 1 USD = 1.36 CAD (example)

### Mistake 3: Missing State Tax Obligations

Washington has no state income tax, but California/New York do. If you worked in CA:
- CA will tax the US-sourced portion ($45K)
- You can claim CA tax as FTC in Canada too
- File CA Form 540-NR (nonresident)

### Mistake 4: Forgetting About Future Vestings

**Critical:** If you have unvested RSUs when you leave, you'll deal with this *every year* until they fully vest.

**Example:**
- You leave US in 2026
- You still have RSUs vesting in 2027, 2028, 2029
- You must file dual-country returns for 4 years

**Pro Tip:** Some employers (Meta, Amazon) allow **accelerated vesting**. If you're leaving the US, ask HR to vest everything before departure to avoid multi-year complications.

## Real Example: Google H-1B to Canada PR Transition

**Profile:**
- Sarah, Software Engineer at Google Mountain View
- H-1B from 2022-2025 (3 years)
- Moved to Toronto Jan 2026 (Canadian PR approved)
- 4-year RSU grant: $320K total ($80K/year)

**2026 Tax Situation (Year 4 vesting):**

**Without proper planning:**
- US withholding: $17,600 (22% federal)
- California tax: $7,360 (9.2% rate)
- Canada tax: $28,800 (35% on $80K)
- **Total: $53,760** (67% effective rate)

**With treaty optimization:**
- US tax (75% allocation): $17,600 on $60K
- Canada tax: $28,800 minus $17,600 FTC = $11,200
- **Total: $28,800** (36% effective rate)
- **Savings: $24,960**

**Where the savings came from:**
1. Claimed Article XV treaty benefit (reduced US taxable from $80K to $60K)
2. Claimed full Foreign Tax Credit in Canada
3. Filed CA Form 540-NR to allocate state tax properly

## Strategic Tax Planning for Multi-Year Vestings

### Option 1: Accelerate Vesting Before Leaving

**Pros:**
- One-time tax hit in US (known rates)
- No future dual-country filings
- Simpler recordkeeping

**Cons:**
- Higher tax bracket in vesting year
- Lose time value of money (paying tax early)

**Best for:** Senior engineers with $500K+ unvested RSUs

### Option 2: Spread Vesting Across Both Countries

**Pros:**
- Lower marginal rates (income spread over years)
- FTC reduces Canada tax burden
- Keep US withholding (forced savings)

**Cons:**
- Must file dual-country returns for 4 years
- Complex recordkeeping
- CPA fees: $1,500-$3,000/year

**Best for:** Mid-level engineers with $200K-$400K unvested

### Option 3: Negotiate Cash Buyout

Some employers offer to buy out unvested equity when you leave. You receive cash equal to current fair market value.

**Tax treatment:**
- Treated as W-2 wages (ordinary income)
- US withholding: 22-37%
- All taxable in US (no Canada split)

**Best for:** Workers moving to low-tax countries (e.g., Dubai)

## When to Hire a Cross-Border Tax Specialist

DIY is feasible if:
- Total RSU income <$150K/year
- No AMT complications
- No state tax issues (WA, TX, FL)
- You're comfortable with tax forms

**Hire a CPA if:**
- Total RSU income >$300K/year
- You have ISOs + RSUs (AMT trap)
- You lived in CA/NY/MA (complex state tax)
- You're applying for Canadian PR (immigration tax issues)

**Average CPA cost:** $2,500-$5,000/year for dual-country filing

## Action Checklist

**Before leaving the US:**
- [ ] Request work location records from HR (badge swipes, office assignments)
- [ ] Download all RSU vesting schedules from stock portal (E*TRADE, Fidelity, Schwab)
- [ ] Ask employer about accelerated vesting options
- [ ] Calculate projected tax liability using our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator)
- [ ] Open Canadian RRSP account (but don't contribute while US resident!)

**After becoming Canadian resident:**
- [ ] File US Form 1040-NR with Form 8833 (treaty claim)
- [ ] File Canadian T1 with Form T2209 (Foreign Tax Credit)
- [ ] File state return if you worked in CA/NY/MA (Form 540-NR, IT-203, etc.)
- [ ] Save all documentation for 7 years (IRS + CRA audit period)

**Each subsequent year until RSUs fully vest:**
- [ ] Update work location tracker
- [ ] Recalculate US vs Canada allocation
- [ ] File dual-country returns by deadlines (US: April 15, Canada: April 30)
